facebookGoLiveTitle: How to go live on Facebook

facebookStartStreamStep: Now start the live from Orbis: the stream goes into the broadcast that is already waiting.
facebookKeyLifetime: A Facebook stream key is good for one day only: take a new one for every live.

lowLatencyHelp: Asks the encoder for the smallest delay it can manage: no lookahead, no scenecut. Turn it off for a re-stream, where the pacing is already done downstream.
adaptiveBitrateHelp: When the network does not carry the live, the bitrate goes down to what it carries and climbs back after a few minutes of clean streaming. Off, the live always goes out at the bitrate above, whatever the network does.
tuningRequired: Without low latency the encoder is tuned by hand: choose a preset and a tune.
youtubeOffAirHelp: The signal is being sent, but Orbis cannot find a public broadcast on the channel. Follow the YouTube checks below; this alone proves neither a fault nor a successful launch.
youtubeUnverifiedHelp: YouTube did not return a verifiable page; this does not prove the broadcast is offline. Orbis also checks the direct live address and keeps the video paused. Check the correct channel in Studio; use its handle (@yourchannel) or channel ID (UC…).
ffmpegSenderHelp: ffmpeg keeps the live at real time and publishes it over its own RTMPS.

encoderQualityHelp: How much work the encoder puts into every frame. Automatic: when the live starts Orbis tests this PC for a few seconds and uses Balanced (NVENC p4) only if the GPU or CPU keeps up with room to spare, Light (p1) otherwise. Light uses less but shows less detail at the same bitrate; High needs a powerful GPU or CPU. A preset chosen in the additional options takes precedence.
encoderQualityHint: Automatic tests this PC and decides by itself: keep it if you are not sure.

youtubeCheckIntro: Orbis checks the public channel. Stream keys alone cannot read or change your Studio settings. Follow these steps before retrying.
youtubeCheckStep1: Open YouTube Studio with the correct account. Select an event that has not ended and compare its stream key with the channel configuration in Orbis. Stop any other encoder using that key.
youtubeCheckStep2: If sending one stream, use Auto for the vertical version or turn off Dual stream before starting. Dual stream in Encoder mode requires a separate vertical feed and its matching key; one Orbis destination sends one feed.
youtubeCheckStep3: Enable Auto-start, or press Go live in Studio when the preview is ready. If you need to reconnect without ending the event, turn off Auto-stop.
youtubeCheckStep4: Start Orbis: it sends a static picture and silence during verification without consuming your video. The content starts only when a live broadcast is found on YouTube. Excellent connection only confirms signal reception. You can use Check YouTube again.
youtubeCheckStep5: Orbis tries up to 3 connections, for up to 60 seconds each, keeping the video paused. If verification still fails, it stops and preserves the position. Recheck Dual stream, the key and Auto-start in Studio; if the event ended, create a new one before retrying.
youtubeCheckStep6: Use Show live and check audio and moving video. Private or unlisted events may be absent from the public channel: open their viewer link in Studio. A public-channel lookup cannot confirm which stream key feeds a video when several events are live.
youtubeVerified: Live found on the YouTube channel
youtubeCheckFailed: YouTube could not be checked. Try again or open Studio.
